sentences: IM7-UNT-L1, unnotched tension, under a displacement of 1 mm along the coupon: the top grip carries 1.622e+04 N, in tension.
The largest displacement is 1 mm at node 274 (0, 194 mm), mostly along the coupon.

The largest ply stresses, each in its own ply's fibre axes, are sigma_1 along the fibres = 1201 MPa in ply 2 (0 degrees) at element 219, sigma_2 across the fibres = 62.85 MPa in ply 4 (90 degrees) at element 229, tau_12 in-plane shear = 45.82 MPa in ply 3 (-45 degrees) at element 213; these are element centroids in the ply's axes, not the global-axis values a viewer such as PrePoMax shows.

The laminate does not exceed the Tsai-Hill criterion at the applied loading: the first ply to fail would be ply 4 (90 degrees), tied with ply 5, at element 67, at the edge of a gripped tab, by the combined stresses (no single component governs), at 1.004 times the applied loading (failure index 0.9957). That element touches a gripped tab, where the stress is not expected to settle as the mesh is refined: read it as first damage at the grip.

The laminate does not exceed the maximum stress criterion at the applied loading: the first ply to fail would be ply 4 (90 degrees), tied with ply 5, at element 67, at the edge of a gripped tab, by tension across the fibres (sigma_2 reaching F2t, a matrix-dominated mode), at 1.019 times the applied loading (failure index 0.9813). That element touches a gripped tab, where the stress is not expected to settle as the mesh is refined: read it as first damage at the grip.
The earliest of the criteria is Tsai-Hill.
As ASTM D3039/D3039M-17 reduces a test: the gross area is 36.58 mm² (25 by 1.463 mm), so the force along the coupon, 1.622e+04 N, is a stress of 443.5 MPa.

The extensometer over 25 mm reads 7289 microstrain, so the chord modulus between 1000 and 3000 microstrain is 60.85 GPa (laminate theory gives 60.85 GPa), and Poisson's ratio is 0.3152 (laminate theory: 0.3152); a linear model gives the same chord over any range.

By Tsai-Hill in the gauge section, the first ply fails at a gross stress of 458.3 MPa: a first-ply-failure stress, not the ultimate strength the standard takes at the maximum force of a test, which a linear model cannot give.
